_comment: The music of the game (see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). dev/music/fetch_music.py downloads each MIDI file or score (checking its license where the site tells it) or reads our own transcription (dev/music/melodies/<slug>.abc), and writes assets/music/<slug>.mid; dev/music/render_music.py renders it into assets/music/<slug>.ogg. instruments maps a track name (or index, or * for all) to an instrument of the renderer; tempo (quarters per minute) replaces the tempo of a score; repeat plays a song several times (e.g., a short song with several verses).

songs.title: Glück auf, der Steiger kommt
songs.about: The traditional song of the miners of the Ore Mountains (Germany)
songs.credit: Melody traditional; set and sequenced by Peter Gerloff (Rabanus Flavus)

songs.title: Oh My Darling, Clementine
songs.about: An American song of the gold rush (1884): the daughter of a miner, forty-niner
songs.credit: Melody traditional; set and sequenced by Peter Gerloff (Rabanus Flavus)

songs.title: Bergmannslied, Op. 4 No. 4
songs.about: A song of the miners by Louise Reichardt (1779-1826) on a poem of Novalis, himself a mining engineer
songs.credit: Louise Reichardt; transcribed by the contributors to OpenScore Lieder

songs.title: Noch ein Bergmannslied, Op. 4 No. 5
songs.about: Another song of the miners by Louise Reichardt (1779-1826) on a poem of Novalis
songs.credit: Louise Reichardt; transcribed by the contributors to OpenScore Lieder

songs.title: In the Hall of the Mountain King, Op. 46 No. 4
songs.about: Edvard Grieg (1843-1907), from Peer Gynt: the trolls in the mountain
songs.credit: Edvard Grieg; typeset by the contributors to the Mutopia Project

songs.title: Troldtog (March of the Dwarfs), Op. 54 No. 3
songs.about: Edvard Grieg (1843-1907), from the Lyric Pieces
songs.credit: Edvard Grieg; typeset by the contributors to the Mutopia Project

songs.title: Lualåt (The Mountaineer's Song), Op. 73 No. 7
songs.credit: Edvard Grieg; typeset by the contributors to the Mutopia Project

songs.title: Cwm Rhondda
songs.about: The Welsh hymn of John Hughes (1873-1932), who started working at a colliery as a boy; sung in the mining valleys of South Wales
songs.credit: John Hughes; typeset by the contributors to the Mutopia Project

songs.title: The Bonny Pit Laddie
songs.about: A traditional song of the coal miners of Northumberland and Durham
songs.credit: Melody traditional, after Bruce and Stokoe, Northumbrian Minstrelsy (1882); our transcription

songs.title: The Collier's Rant
songs.about: A traditional song of the colliers of Tyneside (18th century)
songs.credit: Melody traditional, after Bruce and Stokoe (1882) as printed by R. Palmer; our transcription

songs.title: The Miner's Lifeguard
songs.about: An American song of the miners' union, on the tune of "Life's Railway to Heaven"
songs.credit: Melody by Charles D. Tillman (1890); our transcription

songs.title: Calon Lân
songs.about: The Welsh hymn of John Hughes (1872-1914), sung in the mining valleys of Wales
songs.credit: Melody by John Hughes; our transcription

songs.title: Schon wieder tönt vom Schachte her
songs.about: A traditional German miners' song: the bell of the shaft calls the miners in
songs.credit: Melody traditional, after Erk and Böhme, Deutscher Liederhort (1893), as encoded in the Essen Folksong Collection; our transcription

songs.title: Der Bergmann im schwarzen Gewand
songs.about: A traditional German miners' song from the Deister
songs.credit: Melody traditional, after Böhme, Volksthümliche Lieder der Deutschen (1895), as encoded in the Essen Folksong Collection; our transcription

songs.title: Trimdon Grange Explosion
songs.about: Tommy Armstrong (1848-1920), the pitman poet of Durham, set his song to the traditional air "Go and Leave Me If You Wish It"
songs.credit: Melody traditional, as noted by A. L. Lloyd and printed by R. Palmer; our transcription

songs.title: Bergleut sind die schönsten Leut
songs.about: A traditional German miners' song: the miners are the finest people
songs.credit: Melody traditional, after Erk and Böhme, Deutscher Liederhort (1893), as encoded in the Essen Folksong Collection; our transcription
